canonical_scope: target repository discovery categories used before Alatyr installation, update, or adapter repair

usage.default: Use the smallest category set needed for the selected support profile and enabled modules.
usage.missing_fact: Record unresolved target facts as missing, blocked, deferred, disabled, or not applicable; do not invent them.
usage.detail_owner: Detailed findings belong in the target installation plan and target adapter files, not in this source contract.

profile_selection.expansion_rule: Start with the smallest support profile that preserves safety, routing, source-of-truth ownership, authorization, logical integrity, and evidence. Treat optional modules as explicit expansion unless target evidence or the user request justifies them.

profiles.use_when: The target needs low-cost bootstrap, routing, authorization, logical-integrity, generated entry-packet, support-state, and final-evidence support only.
The target also needs durable engineering evidence, project-knowledge delivery, installed operations, durable approvals, AI infrastructure routing, or consistency-map support.
The target also needs common lifecycle, blueprint/product-change, large-task orchestration, or migration-diff support.
The target needs the complete template surface, selected native assistant bridges, or complete optional-module expansion justified by reviewed target evidence.

base_categories.summary: Target path, install/update state, stack, package/build files, tests, CI, validation entry points, and ownership metadata.
Existing assistant instructions, bridge files, skills, prompts, gates, tool/MCP configuration, source-access policies, and provenance notes.
Canonical project facts, architecture or design documents, decision records, blueprint equivalents, source-of-truth registry, and known conflicts.
Risk classes, approval triggers, current-scope action authorization, destructive/live/credential policies, target commands, and final evidence.
Selected support profile, framework pack, context router, bootstrap index, recursive context indexes, semantic codebook, routed gates, budgets, and receipts.
Support policy, support-state snapshot, generated support surfaces, relationship candidates, reverse indexes, and stale-output handling.
